items.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011
items.q: I can remember Sal Nistico in our music room at home, staying at my house and we were in there playing

ctx.x: Anyway, it’s pretty cool how your son [Rick Montalbano Jr.] has found his way into music. And I bet he was a drummer from an early age.

Yes, from — he was sitting at the drums from when he was an infant he would be on my lap or Jill’s lap, and it was one of the ways — he was a very loud, hyper kid and one of the ways we would calm him down is to put on music and sit him on our lap and put the sticks in his hands and he would just start — and pretty soon it was obvious that he was actually playing the songs. He was playing the melody on the drums you know. So yeah, he showed signs of getting it from very early on. I could never quite get him to go…

over and he did a double take, like what the heck is that, you know, your kid’s playing the drums and we’re playing. We were playing. We weren’t like playing to make him sound good, he was playing with us and it was working. And when he looked over at Ricky, Ricky stuck his tongue out at him. And for days afterwards he would just say “man, what’s with your kid?”
